gloss: to skim over; to read without paying close attention

definitions.gloss: to skim over; to read without paying close attention; to read and let pass
definitions.explanation: To read text superficially without engaging deeply with the content, or to read something and deliberately not react to it.

examples.japanese: {記事|きじ}を{読|よ}み{流|なが}す。
{長|なが}いメールだったので{読|よ}み{流|なが}してしまった。
examples.english: It was a long email, so I just skimmed through it.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{内容|ないよう}だから{読|よ}み{流|なが}さないでちゃんと{読|よ}んでほしい。
examples.english: It's important content, so I'd like you to read it properly and not just skim over it.

notes:
A compound verb of {読|よ}む ('to read') + {流|なが}す ('to let flow, to let pass'). The {流|なが}す component conveys the sense of letting the content 'flow by' without absorbing it. This can be intentional (deliberately not engaging) or unintentional (failing to pay attention).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記事|きじ}を{読|よ}み{流|なが}す: to skim an article
- メールを{読|よ}み{流|なが}す: to skim an email
- さらっと{読|よ}み{流|なが}す: to casually skim through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming, speed reading — a noun describing the act of reading diagonally/quickly
- {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばす: to skip over (parts of text) — implies actively skipping sections entirely
- {流|なが}し{読|よ}み: skimming — a noun with the same meaning, with reversed word order
